key_insight: RM-VLM combines language-generated reward machines with visual proposition grounding to guide reinforcement learning on tasks whose rewards depend on history.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces reliance on hand-engineered observation labelling, making temporally structured reward specifications easier to apply across visual environments.
method: An LLM converts a natural-language task description into a reward machine.
A VLM grounds the machine’s propositions in image observations during policy learning.
A VLM-based value estimator measures progress toward reward-machine transitions to provide dense rewards.
evidence_signal: Across non-Markovian grid-world navigation, robotic manipulation, and 3D object collection, RM-VLM achieved higher task success rates than existing VLM-based reward methods; the abstract provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Incorrect generated reward machines or visual proposition labels could misdirect learning, making validation important before deployment.
paper_title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
